fullPassage: Situational ethics is an ethical theory that takes into account the context of a situation or an act when judging whether it is ethical. Supporters of this theory willingly permit casting aside absolute moral standards. In the absence of a universal standard or law, what matters is the outcome or consequences; so, the end justifies the means. Possibly the following contrasting realities can help illustrate the application of situational ethics. In a pickup game of basketball played among friends, everyone is expected to call his or her own fouls or acknowledge knocking the ball out-of-bounds. Caring about one's friends and maybe getting to keep playing with the group leads to these actions. But, once an organized game is played with officials, most athletes will not admit to the same fouls or violations as the end goal of winning is more important than expressing concern for competitors. Situational ethics has been extended by many athletes and coaches to mean trying to get away with as many actions on the field or court as possible to abandon competitive advantages.

questions.passage: Situational ethics is an ethical theory that takes into account the context of a situation or an act when judging whether it is ethical. Supporters of this theory willingly permit casting aside absolute moral standards. In the absence of a universal standard or law, what matters is the outcome or consequences; so, the end justifies the means. Possibly the following contrasting realities can help illustrate the application of situational ethics. In a pickup game of basketball played among friends, everyone is expected to call his or her own fouls or acknowledge knocking the ball out-of-bounds. __________ and maybe getting to keep playing with the group leads to these actions. But, once an organized game is played with officials, most athletes will not admit to the same fouls or violations as the end goal of winning is more important than expressing concern for competitors. Situational ethics has been extended by many athletes and coaches to mean trying to get away with as many actions on the field or court as possible to abandon competitive advantages.

det.korean: ____하는 것과 계속 경기할 수 있는 것이 이러한 행동으로 이어진다
det.analysis:
❌ ① Competing with one's friends: '친구와 경쟁하다'는 파울 자진신고의 동기가 아님
✅ ② Caring about one's friends: '친구를 배려하다'는 자진신고 동기로 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ Defeating one's opponents: '상대를 이기다'는 공식경기 맥락이지 비공식 친선경기가 아님
❌ ④ Ignoring one's own fouls: '파울을 무시하다'는 파울을 인정하는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: Caring about one's friends = 친구를 배려하는 것

questions.passage: Situational ethics is an ethical theory that takes into account the context of a situation or an act when judging whether it is ethical. Supporters of this theory willingly permit casting aside absolute moral standards. In the absence of a universal standard or law, what matters is the __________; so, the end justifies the means. Possibly the following contrasting realities can help illustrate the application of situational ethics. In a pickup game of basketball played among friends, everyone is expected to call his or her own fouls or acknowledge knocking the ball out-of-bounds. Caring about one's friends and maybe getting to keep playing with the group leads to these actions. But, once an organized game is played with officials, most athletes will not admit to the same fouls or violations as the end goal of winning is more important than expressing concern for competitors. Situational ethics has been extended by many athletes and coaches to mean trying to get away with as many actions on the field or court as possible to abandon competitive advantages.

det.analysis:

❌ ② intention or motivation: '의도나 동기'는 결과가 아닌 과정 초점
✅ ③ outcome or consequences: '결과'가 중요하다는 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ tradition or custom: '전통이나 관습'은 상황 윤리의 결과 중심 논리와 무관
